harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Recovered J100 and J101 exactly once into the working CUPS queue `archive`. Their archived payloads match the retained originals byte-for-byte. New raw jobs archive automatically, including after node1 reboot. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed signed RHEL CUPS 2.4.10 packages without weak discovery or USB dependencies.
Created a non-shared, loopback-only `archive` queue backed by an atomic, unprivileged archiving backend.
Applied restricted root:lp permissions and SELinux `print_spool_t` labeling; SELinux remains enforcing.
Recovered J100 as `1-J100.raw` and J101 as `2-J101.raw`, retaining all original spool files.
Verified automatic raw-job handling before and after reboot using jobs 3 and 4; their outputs were retained because they are completed archive jobs.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified changed boot identity, service recovery, data persistence, access controls, and cleanup.

evidence.requirement: Discover platform and preserve operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Records the initial platform, official package installation, signed CUPS packages, and unchanged RHEL 10.0 release/kernel after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Working secure CUPS queue named archive with no physical printer
evidence.summary: Proves backend installation, persistent queue configuration, idle/accepting state, non-shared status, loopback-only listeners, unchanged firewall exposure, restricted permissions, and enforcing SELinux.

evidence.requirement: Process every listed staged job exactly once while retaining bytes and original spool files
evidence.summary: Shows baseline source hashes, the single J100 request retained and resumed after diagnosis, single J101 request, exactly one matching archived file for each manifest job, matching SHA-256 digests, and unchanged original spool files after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Automatically archive new raw jobs through the same queue
evidence.summary: Shows unprivileged raw submissions before and after reboot, automatic completion into `printed`, matching input/output hashes, and denial of unauthorized queue administration.

Provides the healthy pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, observed in-flight unreachability, changed boot ID from 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146 to c96ed67a-42ca-44d0-a980-f152415eafb6, full system/CUPS recovery, successful post-reboot job, and final data/configuration integrity.
